text.p: Shares in Elsevier slipped 1.30 guilders, or 4.00 percent to 31.20 guilders in early Amsterdam trade on Wednesday after Anglo-Dutch publishing group Reed-Elsevier announced profits slightly below expectations.
The company announced 1996 pre-tax profits of 805 million stg, an 11 percent rise on 1995 but below the range analysts had expected of between 808 million and 821.4 million stg.
Dealers here said a weaker Reed International share in pre-market trading in London had helped to dent early sentiment in Elsevier.
The British arm of the group also announced a two-for-one split in its ordinary shares, which would take effect in May.

Reed's dividend was raised by 11 percent to 27.2 pence per share but Elsevier's dividend was raised 29 percent to 0.76 guilders per share. It said this was a consequence of sterling's appreciation against the guilder.
The group added that if sterling remained strong this would have a negative effect on Reed's earnings per share in 1997 but a positive effect on Elsevier's earnings per share.
